messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing missing spans when correlating Kibana -> Loki in eu-west1. Root trace IDs show up in app stdout but central logs return partial spans and some Loki queries time out (30s+). Prom alerts fired: loki_ingest_cpu_high and loki_query_504_rate. Anyone digging? :thinking_face:

kevin: Which time window? can you paste a trace ID and the query you ran? I can check shard distribution and pod CPU.

maria: Example trace: 7f3a2c9e4b1d6a00. Kibana search shows the application lines but when I run the Loki join I only get the initial span. Loki query I used:
```
{app=\"model-serving\", region=\"eu-west1\"} |= \"trace=7f3a2c9e4b1d6a00\" | json
```
That returns nothing or times out. I see the same trace in the node-level logs on the GPU host though. First seen ~2026-03-15T03:09:00Z.

jin: Likely a hot-shard / write amplification issue. We recently changed structured logging from plain text -> big JSON arrays (see serving v2) so single events are larger and skew ingestion. Hot shard can cause query timeouts and partial visibility. Check compactor backlog and index-rollover metrics: loki_compactor_queue_length, loki_index_frontend_latency.

lena: Grafana panel shows eu-west1 ingesters spiking CPU around 03:10 UTC, and query_frontend pods with many 504s. There's also a burst of high-cardinality labels from gpu nodes: `node_gpu_uuid` and `job_type`.

oliver: We rolled out the v2 structured logs at 03:08 UTC to 20% of serving fleet (canary). That could explain the timing. The structured payloads include big arrays of token-level events — increases event size ~4x for some requests.

kevin: Immediate mitigations I can do now: (1) add a prom relabel rule to drop extremely high-cardinality GPU metrics from Loki ingestion tier for 30m; (2) bump query_frontend timeouts to 60s as a short-term; (3) move a few ingesters out of the eu-west1 hot ring to balance shards. Want me to proceed?

maria: Please do (1) and (3). For (2) let's be careful — longer timeouts hide underlying slowness. Also we need a fix for Kibana -> ES searches returning partial hits; maybe mapping change caused doc routing to prefer older shards.

jin: For prom relabel snippet (quick):
```yaml
- action: drop
  regex: \".*node_gpu_uuid.*\"
  source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_job]
```
That will suppress the extreme labels into Loki ingestion stream while we triage.

lena: For alert tuning: suggest we add a 5m suppression window for loki_query_504_rate and raise the threshold from 3 -> 6 per minute for eu-west1 only. Noise is from the burst, not sustained outage. I'll open a PR to alertmanager.

oliver: I'll roll the v2 change back for the canary subset and remove the large arrays from logs (send them to a separate metrics pipeline instead). Can do a rollback in the next deploy window (10m).

deploy-bot: config change request created by @kevin: prom relabel rule 'drop-high-card-gpu' — awaiting approval.

kevin: Approved, applying now. Also rebalancing two ingesters off eu-west1-hotpool -> will take ~90s.

maria: After the rebalance I'm able to run the Loki query (same trace) and get full spans back. Still seeing a few 504s but much lower. Thanks. I'll file a post-incident note with recommended durable changes: rework structured logs, limit high-card labels at source, add index-hot-shard autosplit rule, and reindex affected segments.

jin: Follow-ups: schedule a compactor tune session (reduce compaction window), and add a kibana/ES preference to prefer local replicas for micro-search to avoid cross-shard tail latency.

lena: I'll update alertmanager config and add a dashboard panel showing per-label-cardinality so we can alert before CPU spikes.

maria: Assigning action items: @kevin - temp relabel + shard rebalance (done), @oliver - rollback canary (triggered), @lena - alert tune + dashboard (PR opened), @jin - compactor tuning (ops doc). I'll write the runbook entry now. Thanks all :white_check_mark:

kevin: leaving a note in #eng-sre-runbooks: \"Hot-loki-shard-gpu-cardinality-2026-03-15\"

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see regression.
